title: Finite open–closed refinement through constructible strata
statement: Let $W$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Suppose finitely many finite partitions of the underlying set of $W$ are given by locally closed subschemes $s_\alpha:S_\alpha\hookrightarrow W$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion], and every stratum image is constructible [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Then each given immersion admits a factorization $S_\alpha\hookrightarrow O_\alpha\hookrightarrow W$ with the first morphism closed, the second open, and both $O_\alpha$ and $O_\alpha\setminus S_\alpha$ quasi-compact. There exists a finite rooted binary tree of locally closed subschemes with root $W$, in which each internal vertex $T$ is partitioned into a quasi-compact open subscheme and its closed complement. Its branches are obtained by scheme-theoretic pullbacks [def-pc-fibre-product] of the chosen immersions $O_\alpha\hookrightarrow W$, $S_\alpha\hookrightarrow O_\alpha$, and their complementary immersions. Every vertex is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, every branch morphism is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and the nonempty leaves partition $W$. For every nonempty leaf $T$ and every original partition there is a stratum $S_\alpha$ of that partition and a morphism $T\to S_\alpha$ whose composite with $s_\alpha$ is the canonical morphism $T\to W$.
